summary: Defines the file layouts used by the ISI TOPS-20 implementation of the Mail Transfer Protocol. It is a companion to the main implementation description.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 785 defines the files that TOPS-20 mail software creates for MTP. A control file lists delivery paths and points to a second file that contains the message.

questions: what is the mtp control file format
how many files does mtp use per message
what files did tops-20 mtp use
subtitle: The file formats connecting TOPS-20 mail creation programs to MTP.

tldr.problem: Mail creation software needs a precise file interface for handing outgoing mail to the TOPS-20 Mail Transfer Protocol implementation.
tldr.mechanism: Each message uses a control file containing the source and recipient paths plus a pointer to a separate file containing the mail text.
tldr.outcome: The RFC defines a two-file handoff that carries multiple recipients without making separate copies of the message text for each one.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 785's status as Unknown. The RFC documents a file interface for one ISI TOPS-20 MTP implementation.

sections.title: A File-Based Handoff to MTP
sections.content:
The document defines the TOPS-20 interface between a mail creation system and the Mail Transfer Protocol in terms of files. It says readers seeking the full MTP protocol should consult RFC 780.

For each piece of mail, the interface uses two files in the directory of the user who created it. The control file has a required name pattern; the mail-text file is strongly suggested to use a matching pattern, though the creating system may choose its actual name.
sections.plainLanguage: A mail program hands a message to MTP by creating two files. One describes delivery, and the other contains the mail.

sections.title: What the Control File Contains
sections.content:
The control file is an ASCIZ text file. It begins with FILE: and the full name of the mail-text file, followed by FROM: and the source path. Each recipient is then listed on its own TO: line.

The file name includes the directory and generation number. The source and destination paths use angle brackets and follow the path definitions in the MTP specification.
sections.plainLanguage: The control file points to the mail text, names the sender, and lists each destination. MTP uses these lines to know where the message should go.

sections.title: One Text File for the Message
sections.content:
The second file contains the mail text in the format described by RFC 733, including its header and body. The control file refers to this file rather than copying its contents into each recipient entry.

Older mail creation systems made a separate text-file copy for each address in the To, Cc, and Bcc fields. With the MTP interface, the same message text file can be referenced from one control file that lists all its recipients.
sections.plainLanguage: The message body and header stay together in one file. The control file can list several recipients without making a separate message copy for each one.
